name: FormFactor, Inc.
sector: Semiconductors / Wafer test equipment (probe cards & systems)
moat_justification: #1 global probe-card supplier (~22-25% share, TechInsights #1 in Test Subsystems 13 consecutive years) with per-device qualification stickiness and a MEMS technology lead in HBM/advanced packaging — but the measured franchise is weaker than the position: ROIC proxy ran only 4.9%-13.1% over FY2020-25 and fell to 4.9% in FY2025, GAAP gross margin was flat ~39-42% for five straight years (pricing power unproven until the 2026 AI cycle), Technoprobe is a strong #2, and demand from a concentrated memory/logic customer base is violently cyclical (revenue -11% in FY2023; conservative OE negative in 2 of the last 3 FYs). Moderate/narrow moat: 5/10.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
LOW_OE_YIELD: base OE yield 1.2% — valuation rests almost entirely on growth; tier is fragile
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 6.4x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Real AI/HBM wafer-test franchise, moat 5/10, but at $105.01 the price embeds far more than even the super-bull owner's-earnings path delivers — weighted IRR 4.52%, weighted IV@15% $15.10 vs $105.01; it clears a 15% hurdle only near $15.
moat_for: #1 global probe-card supplier (~22-25% share; TechInsights #1 in Test Subsystems for 13 consecutive years)
Probe cards are qualified per device and process — requalification friction makes incumbency sticky at TSMC, Samsung, Intel and the memory makers
MEMS / advanced-probe technology lead for HBM and advanced packaging; reported second-source position for Nvidia GPU probe cards at TSMC (Deutsche Bank initiation, Sept 2026)
Net-cash balance sheet (net debt -$91.1M) funds the Farmers Branch capacity build through the cycle
moat_against: ROIC proxy only 4.9%-13.1% FY2020-25 and falling to 4.9% in FY2025 — returns near, not well above, the cost of capital
GAAP gross margin flat ~39-42% for five straight years — no proven pricing power until the 2026 AI/HBM cycle
Technoprobe is a strong #2 (~16% share), plus Micronics Japan, MPI and low-cost Chinese entrants
Customer concentration in a handful of memory/logic makers; violently cyclical demand (revenue -11% in 2023, conservative OE negative in 2 of last 3 FYs)
SBC consumes most of pre-SBC cash generation in soft years (engine F sub-type 'sbc_exceeds_cash' on the median window)
